Existing tests under `tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/` pass; any test changed because it pinned the old Polars behaviour is listed in the landing report.

Reference-answer and equivalence tests that the unit and fast tiers run for TPC-DS, TPC-H, TPC-Havoc, ClickBench and CoffeeShop on Polars pass unchanged (checked by the leader on the integration tree).

Timing gate, Polars only, at SF1 and SF10 where the benchmark has that scale locally: TPC-H Q16, TPC-DS Q16, ClickBench Q5 and Q9, CoffeeShop order-count query, measured as described in the context. The outcome is recorded in context before the final PR is armed.
`make batch-member-check TESTS=<the new test file>` passes on the member head; `make comment-policy-check` reports no finding for the touched files.
A `changelog.d/` fragment states that Polars distinct counts now ignore NULL, matching SQL and the other DataFrame platforms.
context:
Timing method: compare the batch start head (base) with the member head on the locked engine versions (record `polars`, `datafusion`, `pyspark` versions). Run base and member alternately, one warm-up then five timed runs each, and compare the best time per cell. A cell is one query on one platform at one scale factor. Scale factors SF1 and SF10; platforms polars-df, datafusion-df, pyspark-df unless stated otherwise. For this item the platform is polars-df only, because other platforms' code does not change.

Evidence so far: Polars 1.44.2 returns n_unique 2 for {1, NULL} and 1 for {NULL, NULL}. Q28 in TPC-DS already filters NULL before `n_unique()`; it stays as it is (owned by no member).

Known and left alone: `benchbox/core/read_primitives/dataframe_queries.py` calls Polars `n_unique()` directly on `o_custkey` (TPC-H data, no NULL). It is outside this member's scope. `tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_unified_frame_coverage.py` uses a fake native expression; it may need the new method the implementation calls.
description:
Problem. `UnifiedExpr.n_unique()` in `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py` maps to `countDistinct` on PySpark and `count(distinct)` on DataFusion, which skip NULL, and to Polars `n_unique()`, which counts NULL as one value. Benchmark DataFrame queries call it wherever the SQL says `COUNT(DISTINCT x)`: about 50 sites across TPC-DS, TPC-H, TPC-Havoc, Data Vault, read primitives, CoffeeShop, AMPLab, ClickBench, FlightData and TSBS DevOps. The same query can therefore return a different count on Polars than on the other platforms and than the SQL when `x` holds NULL. Only TPC-DS data is known to contain NULLs in such a column; FlightData is real data and unverified.

Change. On the Polars path, `n_unique()` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values, in aggregation, group-by and over-window contexts. PySpark and DataFusion paths are unchanged.

Decision gate (implementation form, decided by the timing gate, by the leader):
- Start with dropping NULLs before counting.
- PASS: no Polars cell is more than 10% slower than base -> keep it.
- FAIL: any cell is more than 10% slower -> switch to counting distinct values and subtracting one when the group contains a NULL, then time again. If that is also more than 10% slower on any cell, stop and ask the owner; do not land a slower shared method.

Frozen scope: `benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py`, `tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/**`.

Guardrails (all members of batch df-distinct-remediation):
- Stay inside the frozen scope listed below; a path outside it is refused at landing.
- No platform-name branch may select a query pattern. One rule for every platform.
- Do not edit SQL query text, reference answers, expected-result fixtures, or equivalence baselines to make a check pass. A changed answer is a defect in the change.
- No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). No new helper before `make duplicate-check-delta` shows no equivalent.
- Members make no tracker call of any kind, open no PR, and do not run the fast tier. They use absolute paths under their own worktree and stop at a landing report.
- Timing runs only through `make heavy-run CMD='...'` after `make heavy-status`, on an idle machine: 1-minute load average at or below 3.0 before every pass. A pass that starts or ends above that is discarded, not averaged in.
- Timing harness scripts are throwaway and are not committed; results go under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/df-distinct-remediation/ and are summarised in this item's context.
- Do not edit any benchmark query module; call sites keep calling `n_unique()`.
- Do not change `approx_n_unique()` or the pandas-family code.
- If an existing test asserts that Polars counts NULL, that test pinned the defect: update it to the SQL meaning and say so in the landing report.
